 S/o Ramakrishna,

 D.O. 6th floor, Krushi Bhavan,

 Bengaluru - 560001.

 Scch-1 2 Mvc No.4705/2023
 Judgment

Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EV-4363 asserting that on 19.03.2017 at 12.30 p.m. when traveling by sitting on the pillion of a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06- EV-4363 rode by Anil Kumar from Heggadathihalli village towards Santemavathuru, near Hegadathihalli village, Kunigal Taluk, Anil kumar negligently rode the motorcycle, made the motorcycle to turn turtle, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Lakkamma vs Anilkumar on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105434446/
1 2.

Petitioner took treatment at Government Hospital, Kunigal and Sapthagiri Hospital, Bengaluru,
as on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 45 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/per month by working as a Coolie.
3. Regarding accident Huliyurdurga police registered crime No.60/2017 against the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EV-4363.
4. In spite of service of the notice, respondent No.1 - owner of the motorcycle remained absent.

5. In response to the notice, respondent No.2 appeared through his Advocate, filed written statement, denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, age, occupation, income,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 08.08.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that

on 19.03.2017 at about 12.30 p.m., on Amruthuru Santheymavatturu main road, Kunigal Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, in view of the negligent use of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-ED-4363 accident taken place resulting in the injuries to the petitioner?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order ?
7.

On 24.09.2024, 07.11.2024, 06.02.2025 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 10 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.10.
8.
I have heard arguments submitted on behalf of respondent No.2- insurance company and perused the records.

9. On the basis of the records, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the affirmative Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.37,900/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation from the respondents.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 19.03.2017 at 12.30 p.m. when traveling by sitting on the pillion of a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EV-4363 rode by Anil Kumar from Lakkamma vs Anilkumar on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105434446/
2

Heggadathihalli village towards Santemavathuru, near Hegadathihalli village, Kunigal Taluk, Anil kumar negligently rode the motorcycle, made the motorcycle to turn turtle, thereby caused accident,
caused injuries to the petitioner.
11. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
12. In the cross-examination nothing has been asked to petitioner reason and mode the accident.

13. Ex.P.3 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.60/2017 registered by Huliyurdurga police, against respondent No.1- Anil kumar - rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EV-4363 having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint presented by Gangadhara M.N. S/o Late Nanjegowda.

Ex.P.4 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Huliyurdurga police, in crime No.60/2017 against respondent No.1- Anil kumar - rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EV-4363 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of the IMV report.

Ex.P.7 is the copy of the Discharge Summary in which reason for the injuries suffered by the petitioner is noted as RTA.
14.
In this case respondents have not placed any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of the accident.

Hence I have concluded that on 19.03.2017 at 12.30 p.m. when petitioner was traveling by sitting on the pillion of a motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EV-4363 rode by Anil Kumar ( son of the petitioner) from Heggadathihalli village towards Santemavathuru, near Hegadathihalli village, Kunigal Taluk, Anil kumar negligently rode the motorcycle, made the motorcycle to turn turtle, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident she has suffered injuries, took treatment at Community Health Center, Kunigal, then at Sapthagiri Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient for a period of 7 days, by spending Rs.50,000/-.
Petitioner stated that as on the date of accident being aged about 45 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/-per month by working as Labour.
16. In the written statement, respondent No.2- insurance company denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
17. In the cross-examination petitioner admitted that in the wound certificate and charge sheet nature of the injuries suffered by her are noted as simple.
Petitioner admitted that medical bills produced at Ex.P.8 are not supported by prescriptions.
18. Discharge summary shows that in the accident petitioner suffered laceration wound over right knee, took treatment at Sapthagiri Hospital, Bengaluru as inpatient from 19.03.2017 to 25.03.2017.
In the copy of Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.9 the date of birth of the petitioner is noted as 04.07.1972.
The medical bills shows that petitioner spent Rs.7,902/- towards treatment charges.

sentences.text: In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding the nature of the injuries suffered in the accident, length, place and treatment taken for those injuries.

Hence, I award Rs.10,000/- towards pain and sufferings,
Rs.7,900/- towards treatment charges, Rs.10,000/- towards attendant, conveyance, nourishment charges, Rs.10,000/- towards loss of income during treatment period and loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
20.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.37,900/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. as compensation.
21. The copy of the policy marked at Ex.P.1 shows that as on the date of accident motorcycle bearing No.KA-06- EV-4363 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2- insurance company.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident respondent No.1- rider/owner of the motorcycle has violated any terms of the policy.
22. The record shows that on 05.10.2023 insurance company appeared through his advocate, then on 09.01.2024 filed written statement.

Hence, I have inferred that on technical ground of delay etc.
it is neither fit nor proper to deny the compensation to the petitioner who suffered minor injuries in the alleged accident.

Hence I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EV- 4363 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.37,900/- (Rupees Thirty seven thousand nine hundred only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-06-EV-4363 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the11th day of April, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
